entities.summary: Andrea Corsini was an Italian Catholic prelate and professed member from the Carmelites who served as the Bishop of Fiesole from 1349 until his death. Born in Florence, Italy, around 1310, Corsini was ordained as a priest at a young age and quickly rose through the ranks of the Carmelite Order. In 1349, he was elected as the Bishop of Fiesole, a position he held until his death in 1374. During his tenure, Corsini oversaw the rebuilding of Fiesole after the devastating effects of the Black Death, which had ravaged the region in the late 14th century. He also played a key role in the establishment of the University of Florence, which would go on to become one of the most prestigious institutions of higher learning in Europe. Corsini's legacy extends beyond his religious leadership, as he was also a patron of the arts and a supporter of the city's economic development. His commitment to the well-being of his people and the advancement of his faith earned him a place in the annals of Italian history.
